# Rainfall product comparison: CHIRPS vs IMERG

<!-- Generated by scripts/compare_rainfall_products.py — do not edit by hand. -->

## What was compared, and on what

- **UCSB CHIRPS v2.0 Final**: 325,710 district-days, 2015-01-01 to 2026-07-31
- **NASA IMERG Final Run v07**: 302,302 district-days, 2015-01-01 to 2025-09-30
- **Common support**: 302,302 district-days, 3,926 days x 77 districts, 2015-01-01 to 2025-09-30
- District-days in UCSB CHIRPS v2.0 Final only: 23,408 (the product's later record, which has no IMERG counterpart)

The products cover different periods. Comparing their full records would confound product with period, because the non-overlapping tail is a seasonally non-random slice. Every statistic below is computed on district-days present in both series.

## Agreement on exceeding 51.6 mm at R5

This is the comparison that matters operationally: not whether the two products report the same millimetres, but whether they make the same call on the same district-day.

| | B exceeds | B does not |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| **A exceeds** | 31,369 | 14,192 |
| **A does not** | 16,986 | 239,447 |

- Exceedance rate, UCSB CHIRPS v2.0 Final: 0.1509
- Exceedance rate, NASA IMERG Final Run v07: 0.1601
- Percentage agreement: 0.8968
- Cohen's kappa: 0.607

## Excluding the two districts with almost no IMERG grid support

Bhaktapur resolves to one 0.1-degree cell and Kathmandu to three, so their IMERG 'district means' are close to point measurements. Removing them leaves 294,150 district-days at R5:

- ratio of means (B/A): 1.139
- Spearman: 0.782
- Cohen's kappa on exceedance: 0.609

## Caveats carried into the manuscript

1. UCSB CHIRPS v2.0 Final district means are area-weighted (ClimateSERV, server-side); NASA IMERG Final Run v07 district means are unweighted means of 0.1-degree cell centres inside each district. This comparison therefore differs in aggregation as well as in product.
2. Bhaktapur (1 grid cell) and Kathmandu (3) have almost no spatial support in IMERG and should be caveated in any per-district reading.
3. This comparison establishes how the two products differ **as measurements**. Whether the threshold itself is product-dependent is a separate question, answered by re-estimating it on IMERG over this same period with an identically truncated CHIRPS run as the control.
